---
name: phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline
description: The project's phase order — microbenchmarks ended 2026-09-13 for the z-image slice; z-image parked 2026-09-14 for the speech verticals; parakeet finished, kokoro next.
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-13 Oliver chose to end the microbenchmark phase and build the
**z-image-turbo vertical slice** (loader → DiT → attention → VAE → PNG) with
real weights, accepting ~20-30 s/image at first. Image generation is the
priority model of the five in `GOALS.md`. Kernel work now continues only
where a profiler points, not where the IDEAS backlog points.

**Why:** after 15+ sessions, `bench/` was 84% of the Go code, every `api/`
endpoint returned `NotImplemented`, no checkpoint had ever been loaded (all
results were against random tensors), and the last iteration bought 1.09x
while attention and convolution sat at zero. The backlog generates new items
faster than it closes them, so it has no convergence criterion.

**How to apply:** prefer finishing a runnable stage over optimising a
measured one. Validate each stage against the diffusers reference rather
than a shape table — that is also what unblocks IDEAS §7 (accuracy), which
has zero work done and gates every format decision.

**Update 2026-09-14:** the z-image slice reached `prompt → PNG` in 14.26 s and
is now **parked**, with its resume points at the top of `PIPELINE.md`. Oliver's
call was to take the two simpler verticals first — speech-to-text
(`parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`) and text-to-speech (`Kokoro-82M`) — and come back for
the remaining z-image performance after. The current plan lives in
**`SPEECH.md`**, which is now the file to read first.

**Update 2026-09-14 (later):** the **parakeet vertical is finished** — S1-S8,
mel to transcript with the whole model resident on the device, 43 ms for an
11 s clip at 257x real time against 2.68 s on the CPU. `SPEECH.md` is still
the file to read first; next is kokoro (T1-T5) and, because it is now 48% of
the clip, the mel front end.

See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] for how to run the old benchmark suite, and
[[auto-committer-owns-main]] for why the commit log is not the project's
narrative.
===
---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, LLM.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, LLM.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].

content.text:
**I7 is done — `/v1/images/edits` answers, over SDEdit.**

## What was built

- **`zimage/vae/encoder.go`** — the CPU encoder, the decoder's mirror. `Conv2D` gained `Stride` and `PadEnd` for diffusers' `(0,1,0,1)` downsampler, plus a `DiagonalGaussian` head (`Mode` takes the mean; sampling would break seed reproducibility).
- **`zimage/vae/gpu_encoder.go`** + `shaders/vae_downsample2x.comp` — the Vulkan graph, 122 dispatches, reusing every stage-7/8 kernel. `attn`/`gemm` moved onto the shared `engine` so the mid block is literally the same code in both directions. Added **`GPUEncoder.RunTo`**, the encoder's `GPUBlock.RunTo`.
- **`zimage/pipeline`** — `Options.Encoder`, `Request.Init`/`Strength`, `StartStep`, `DecodeLatent`. An edit is the *same loop* with a different starting index.
- **`api` / `backend` / `cmd/serve`** — an edit is a field on `ImageRequest`, not a second method, so streaming, `n`, seeds and partials came for free. Multipart **and** JSON. New `-edits` flag, `backend/resize.go` for cover-crop fitting.
- **`cmd/zimage -init/-strength`**, **`cmd/vaebench -encode`**, `reference/dump_vae_encoder.py`, `reference/dump_zimage_edit.py`.

## Two findings worth your attention

**1. Stage 8's fp16 precondition is necessary but not sufficient, and the encoder is the counterexample.** It passes the range test with *more* headroom than the decoder (284 vs 497, 231× inside fp16) and was still 0.58 out at the latent. Not a shader bug — simulating the narrowing on the CPU reproduced the GPU's number to four figures. The encoder *contracts*, amplifying a `conv_in` perturbation by ~4e5, and diffusers' own float32 does the same (6.3e-4 from its float64). I kept the fast path (**425 ms vs 1.78 s**) because the right metric for a latent is relative L2 — 2.2e-2, and **4.2e-4 of a [-1,1] range once decoded**, a twentieth of an 8-bit level. The fp32 graph stays as oracle and is selectable.

**2. The stride-2 convolution needed no kernel.** A 3×3 stride-2 conv under that asymmetric pad computes exactly what the stride-1 pad-1 form computes at the odd pixels — so it runs on the unmodified kernel and discards three pixels in four. 18 ms of a 425 ms encode, asserted on the real filter with a negative control at 32000× the bound.

**And the question `IMAGE.md` said was unmeasured: yes, an 8-NFE turbo distillation edits fine via SDEdit.** Strength is monotone (0.073 floor → 0.178/0.291/0.376/0.630/1.441), composition matches diffusers at **1.06e-2** — better than a generation's 2.2e-2, because six of eight steps of compounding never happen. A 1024² edit at default strength is **11.3 s** vs 14.3 for a generation; 512² over HTTP is **2.5 s**.

Everything is green (`go build`/`vet`/`gofmt` clean, all tests pass). Docs updated: `IMAGE.md` rewritten, `API.md`'s last flagless refusal gone, `research/i7-vae-encoder-and-edits.md` written.

One thing I decided rather than asked: **`mask` is refused with a 501** that explains it's per-step latent blending, a different mechanism. You asked for SDEdit specifically, and `GOALS.md` doesn't ask for edits at all — but it's now the only missing piece of that endpoint, so say the word if you want it.
